package.name: Triveni Sangam

research.recognisable_features: Visible line where the paler, silt-laden Ganga meets the greener, darker Yamuna; wide sandbanks; wooden pilgrim boats clustered at the meeting point
research.dominant_landscape: Broad flat river floodplain with sandbars
research.key_landmark: The confluence itself, with the Allahabad Fort walls on the Yamuna bank nearby
research.surroundings: Open sandy floodplain, ghats and boat landings, the city of Prayagraj beyond the Yamuna bank
research.uncertainties: Exact boat count and any temporary mela infrastructure vary by season; shown as an ordinary non-mela morning

package.geographic_description: Confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna on the eastern edge of Prayagraj in the Gangetic plain; the Saraswati is traditionally believed to join invisibly.
package.primary_subject: The meeting line of the two rivers with pilgrim boats gathered at the confluence point
package.drone_viewpoint: Over the Ganga, south-east of the confluence, looking north-west so the colour seam runs diagonally toward the fort and city
package.lighting: Low, soft sunlight raking across the water, long shadows from boats on the sand, gentle specular highlights on the river surface
package.weather: Calm winter morning, light river mist thinning over the water, pale hazy sky
package.environmental_details: Wide pale sandbars, a few dozen wooden rowing boats with small canopies, modest groups of pilgrims on boats, bamboo poles marking bathing spots
package.composition: Colour seam on a diagonal from lower left; confluence point at the right third; fort and city low on the horizon; soft mist-filled sky in the upper left for text
package.visual_description: A wide morning aerial of two rivers of different colours meeting, small wooden boats gathered where they join, sandbanks in the foreground and Prayagraj's fort and skyline hazy in the distance.
package.image_prompt: Aerial photograph of Triveni Sangam at Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, where two rivers of different colour meet. The pale, silt-laden, sandy-grey Ganga and the darker, greener Yamuna flow side by side and meet along a sharp, slightly wavering diagonal seam traced by a thin line of foam, swirls and small eddies, the dominant feature of the frame. About thirty weathered wooden rowing boats with faded canvas canopies, each slightly different, cluster near the meeting point, some tied together, a few moving and leaving small wakes, carrying small groups of pilgrims seen as tiny figures. In the foreground a broad pale sandbar with fine wind ripples, damp tide-lines, footprints, bamboo poles and a rope line at a boat landing; across the Yamuna the long sandstone ramparts of Allahabad Fort, and beyond them the low hazy skyline of Prayagraj. Shot from 140 m above the Ganga, camera tilted 35° downward, 28mm lens. Early winter morning, low sun from the right, long soft boat shadows, river mist lifting from the water, pale hazy sky.
package.alt_text: Aerial view of Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, India
package.image_description: Morning aerial view of the Ganga and Yamuna meeting at Triveni Sangam, their different water colours forming a seam, with wooden boats gathered at the confluence and Prayagraj hazy beyond.
package.website_caption: Triveni Sangam viewed from above, where the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati are traditionally believed to meet.

package.name: Jaisalmer Fort

research.recognisable_features: Honey-yellow sandstone ramparts with dense rounded bastions wrapping Trikuta Hill; a living fort packed with houses, havelis and Jain temples
research.dominant_landscape: Flat Thar Desert plain around a low rocky hill
research.key_landmark: The fort's ring of bastions and the old town inside its walls
research.surroundings: Jaisalmer town of flat-roofed yellow sandstone houses at the foot of the hill, open scrub desert beyond

package.geographic_description: Twelfth-century fort crowning Trikuta Hill above the town of Jaisalmer in the Thar Desert of western Rajasthan.
package.primary_subject: The bastioned outer walls of Jaisalmer Fort and the dense settlement within
package.drone_viewpoint: South-west of the hill, looking north-east across the bastions with the town spreading below
package.lighting: Warm low sun modelling every rounded bastion, deep but readable shadows between walls, stone glowing natural honey-yellow without orange cast
package.weather: Dry clear air with light desert haze softening the horizon
package.environmental_details: Flat rooftops with water tanks and laundry inside the walls, narrow lanes, sparse khejri and scrub on the slopes, light traffic of cars and motorcycles on the ring road
package.composition: Fort mass on the left two-thirds, town falling away to the lower right, hazy desert horizon with clear sky band at top for text
package.visual_description: A late-afternoon oblique aerial of Jaisalmer's yellow sandstone fort, its many bastions curling around the hilltop, a dense old town inside the walls and flat desert stretching to a hazy horizon.
package.image_prompt: Aerial photograph of Jaisalmer Fort, Rajasthan: a living hilltop citadel of weathered pale straw-yellow sandstone crowning Trikuta Hill above the Thar Desert. A rugged outer wall of rough-cut sandstone blocks traces the rim of the hill, broken into dozens of squat rounded bastions, their faces streaked, chipped and stained darker beneath the parapets. Within the walls hundreds of flat-roofed sandstone houses climb in uneven tiers, divided by narrow shadowed lanes, with carved haveli facades and latticed jharokha balconies, rooftop water tanks, satellite dishes, laundry and parked scooters, and a few small carved Jain temple spires rising slightly above a flat horizontal skyline. Below the hill the town spreads in low, irregular sandstone and sun-faded plaster buildings, a curving road with a few cars, motorcycles and a bus, scattered khejri trees, stony slopes with boulders, then flat beige desert fading into dust haze. Shot from 120 m above, south-west of the hill, camera tilted 30° downward, 32mm lens. Late-afternoon sun from the left, long soft shadows between the bastions, pale hazy sky.
package.alt_text: Aerial view of Jaisalmer Fort in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, India
package.image_description: Late-afternoon aerial view of Jaisalmer Fort's yellow sandstone walls and rounded bastions on Trikuta Hill, with houses packed inside and the flat Thar Desert reaching a hazy horizon.
package.website_caption: Jaisalmer Fort, the 'Golden Fort', is one of the world's few living forts, with homes, shops and temples still inside its sandstone walls.

package.name: Pangong Lake

research.recognisable_features: Long narrow high-altitude lake whose water shifts between turquoise and deep blue, framed by bare brown and ochre mountains
research.dominant_landscape: Arid high-altitude Himalayan trans-range desert at about 4,200 m
research.key_landmark: The lake's long arm receding between mountain ranges toward the east
research.surroundings: Barren scree slopes, gravel shoreline, a dirt road and the small village of Spangmik with a few camps
research.uncertainties: Snow cover on peaks varies by month; shown as early summer with snow only on the highest ridgelines

package.geographic_description: Endorheic high-altitude lake at roughly 4,200 m in eastern Ladakh, stretching about 134 km, with the larger part extending into Tibet.
package.primary_subject: The turquoise-to-blue lake receding between bare mountain ranges
package.drone_viewpoint: Over the western shore near Spangmik, looking east along the length of the lake
package.lighting: Crisp high-altitude sunlight with hard-edged shadows in mountain gullies and saturated but natural water tones
package.weather: Cool, very clear thin air, a few small cumulus clouds over the ranges, slight distance haze
package.environmental_details: Gravel shoreline with shallow turquoise water grading to deep blue, a dirt road tracing the shore, a few flat-roofed houses and white tents of Spangmik, no trees
package.composition: Shoreline curving from the lower left, lake receding to the upper right, mountains filling the middle band, open sky upper left for text
package.visual_description: A wide aerial of Pangong Lake stretching away between bare brown mountains, its water shading from shallow turquoise to deep blue, a dirt road and small village on the near shore.
package.image_prompt: Aerial photograph of Pangong Lake in eastern Ladakh at about 4,200 m: a long, narrow ribbon of water stretching east between bare Himalayan ranges until it fades into haze. Near the shore the water is clear pale green-turquoise over a pebbly bed of grey and ochre stones, then bands into teal and deep slate-blue further out, textured with fine wind ripples; a thin white line of wave wash edges the gravel beach. Steep, angular mountains of fractured grey, brown and rust-coloured rock rise from the water, with layered strata, broken cliffs, long scree slopes, talus fans and dry gullies; a thin dusting of snow lies on the highest distant summit. A narrow dirt track follows the shore past a few low whitewashed flat-roofed Ladakhi houses with firewood stacked on the roofs, a cluster of small canvas tents and one dusty SUV casting a sharp shadow. Shot from 160 m above the western shore near Spangmik, camera tilted 20° downward, 24mm lens. Mid-morning sun from the right, hard shadows in the gullies, thin clear air, pale washed-out sky with a few thin clouds.
package.alt_text: Aerial view of Pangong Lake in Ladakh, India
package.image_description: Mid-morning aerial view along Pangong Lake, its water shifting from turquoise shallows to deep blue between bare brown Ladakhi mountains, with a dirt road and small village on the shore.
package.website_caption: Pangong Lake, at about 4,200 m in Ladakh, shifts through shades of blue and stretches across the border into Tibet.
